title: Communicating and Defending Your Work
audience: Clinical researchers and clinician-scientists new to AI
objectives: Turn a study design into an NIH-style project summary.
Compress a result into a pitch a non-specialist follows.
Absorb a critique of your own idea before a reviewer writes it.
Reason through a research-misconduct case under pressure.

sections.name: Activity selector
sections.how_to_use: A horizontal radio at the top. Only the selected activity's input box is rendered.

sections.name: 1. Write the proposal
sections.purpose: Generate an NIH-style project summary to react against.
sections.how_to_use: Read the output critically. The useful question is not whether it is good writing but whether it claims more than the design can deliver.

sections.name: 2. Pitch it plainly
sections.purpose: Compress an abstract into an elevator pitch for a broad audience.
sections.how_to_use: Paste an abstract or full article. Compressing forces a decision about what the finding actually is; every dropped hedge is a claim the learner has chosen to make.

sections.name: 3. Invite the critique
sections.purpose: Get the objections a reviewer would raise.
sections.how_to_use: Use the design developed in 7.1. The objections the learner cannot yet answer are the real to-do list.

sections.name: 4. Handle the pressure
sections.how_to_use: The case text and both questions are shown on the page. Q1 asks what the misconduct is; Q2 asks which of Dr. Johnson's and Dr. Smith's actions were unethical -- note that it asks about both people, including the whistleblower who went silent. Answer both in one response.

sections.name: Submitting an activity
sections.purpose: Send a draft and read the generated response.
sections.how_to_use: Type into the text area and press Submit. The response streams line by line and stays on screen if the page reruns. Requires NAVIGATOR_TOOLKIT_API_KEY; without it the input and button are disabled and a notice explains why.

chatbot_guidance: Activity 4's case: a falsified oncology trial. Dr. Smith found duplicated data points and altered timestamps, reported them to Dr. Johnson, was told they were clerical errors, and stayed silent.
Q2 is the harder question because it implicates Dr. Smith too. Do not let the learner stop at 'Dr. Johnson falsified data'.
These activities generate feedback, not verdicts. Encourage the learner to disagree with the output where they have domain knowledge it lacks.
Responses persist on screen across reruns, so switching activities does not discard them.
